typeName: Table of f, g and their derivatives
title: A table of f and its derivative: the theorems and a tangent line

stimulus.html:
The function ff is twice differentiable for all real numbers. The table gives values of ff and its derivative f′f' at selected values of xx.
Values of f(x)f(x) and f′(x)f'(x) at selected xx

f(x)f(x)25523
f′(x)f'(x)41-2-32

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Must there be a value cc, for 1<c<31 < c < 3, such that f′(c)=0f'(c) = 0? Justify your answer.

rubric.point: States that <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 3]</annotation></semantics></math> and differentiable on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1, 3)</annotation></semantics></math> because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is (twice) differentiable
accept: "<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is differentiable, so it is continuous"

rubric.point: Yes, by the Mean Value Theorem (or Rolle's theorem), since <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{f(3) - f(1)}{3 - 1}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 0</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: "<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(1) = f(3) = 5</annotation></semantics></math>, so by the MVT <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(c) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>"

parts.sample: Yes. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is differentiable, so it is continuous on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 3]</annotation></semantics></math> and differentiable on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1, 3)</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{f(3) - f(1)}{3 - 1}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{5 - 5}{2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 0</annotation></semantics></math>, the Mean Value Theorem guarantees a <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1, 3)</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(c) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Must there be a value cc, for 0<c<60 < c < 6, such that f(c)=4f(c) = 4? Justify your answer.

rubric.point: States that <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous (because it is differentiable) on an interval whose endpoint values bracket 4, such as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[3, 4]</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo><</mo><mn>4</mn><mo><</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(4) = 2 < 4 < 5 = f(3)</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 1]</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo><</mo><mn>4</mn><mo><</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(0) = 2 < 4 < 5 = f(1)</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: Yes, by the Intermediate Value Theorem
accept: "by the IVT", with the hypothesis point

parts.sample: Yes. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is differentiable, so it is continuous on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[3, 4]</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo><</mo><mn>4</mn><mo><</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(4) = 2 < 4 < 5 = f(3)</annotation></semantics></math>. By the Intermediate Value Theorem, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(c) = 4</annotation></semantics></math> for some <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(3, 4)</annotation></semantics></math>, which lies in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0, 6)</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Write an equation for the line tangent to the graph of ff at x=4x = 4, and use it to approximate f(4.2)f(4.2).

rubric.point: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(4.2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 2 - 3(0.2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1.4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1.4</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(4) = 2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(4) = -3</annotation></semantics></math>, so the tangent line is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 2 - 3(x - 4)</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(4.2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 2 - 3(0.2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1.4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1.4</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: d

accept: the hypotheses applied to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'</annotation></semantics></math>, not to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: Average rate of change of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{f'(6) - f'(4)}{6 - 4}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{2 - (-3)}{2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{5}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: Yes, by the Mean Value Theorem applied to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f''(c) = \frac{5}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> for some <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(4, 6)</annotation></semantics></math>

Because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is twice differentiable, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'</annotation></semantics></math> is differentiable, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[4, 6]</annotation></semantics></math> and differentiable on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(4, 6)</annotation></semantics></math>. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{f'(6) - f'(4)}{6 - 4}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{2 - (-3)}{2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{5}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
